name: layers

# The Layers

.small[
| Layer | Path | Who writes | Loaded |
|---|---|---|---|
| Managed policy | `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md` | an organization | every session |
| **User (global)** | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.claude/rules/*.md` | you | every session, every project |
| **Project** | `./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md` | you, via git | every session in the repo |
| Project local | `./CLAUDE.local.md` (gitignored) | you | with the project file |
| Project rules | `./.claude/rules/*.md` | you, via git | every session, or on demand with `paths:` |
| Subdirectory | `<subdir>/CLAUDE.md` | you | when Claude touches a file there |
| **Auto memory** | `~/.claude/projects/<key>/memory/` | Claude | index every session; topic files on demand |
]

--

Module 2 was about writing these well. This module: where they live, how they load, what goes in which, and how they go missing.

---

# How the Instruction Files Load

Every `CLAUDE.md` and `CLAUDE.local.md` from the filesystem root **down to** the working directory, concatenated. The file closest to where you launched is read last.

--

Within one directory, `CLAUDE.local.md` is appended after `CLAUDE.md`.

--

A subdirectory's `CLAUDE.md` loads once Claude reads, writes or edits a file in it. A `cat` of one file counts as a read.

--

**Nothing overrides anything.** It is all concatenated. Two contradicting lines in different layers are both in context, and the model picks. That is the whole reason `/doctor prompt-audit` exists.

--

`@path/to/file` imports at launch. Organizes a long file; does not make it cheaper.

---
name: rules-paths

# Rules With Paths

`.claude/rules/r-scripts.md`:

```markdown
---
paths:
  - "data/**/*.R"
---
# R scripts in data/
Use base pipes (|>), never magrittr.
Print the excluded-row count before any summary.
```

--

Loads only when Claude works with a matching file. Without `paths:`, a rule loads every session like `CLAUDE.md`.

--

`~/.claude/rules/` holds the same thing for every project. The directory accepts symlinks, so one shared rule set can be linked into several repos (an approval dialog once per project).

The drill proves the scoping with two headless probes: before and after reading an R file.

---
name: auto-memory

# Auto Memory: Claude's Own Notes

```
~/.claude/projects/<key>/memory/
├── MEMORY.md             # index: one line per memory, loaded every session
├── user_role.md          # type: user
├── feedback_pipes.md     # type: feedback
├── project_deadline.md   # type: project
└── reference_tracker.md  # type: reference
```

--

- The first **200 lines or 25 KB** of `MEMORY.md` load; the rest is dropped. Topic files are read on demand. Near the limit the harness tells Claude to shorten the index.
- Keyed by the **git repository**: worktrees and subdirectories share one store.
- **Machine-local.** Never reaches a cloud session. Not inherited by subagents (a fork excepted).
- `/memory` toggles it; `autoMemoryDirectory` in settings moves it.

--

A wrong inference persists until edited. Read the index now and then.

---

# What Belongs Where

The test: **who else should see it, and when is it needed?**

| It is... | Put it in |
|---|---|
| a rule about how you work, every project | user `CLAUDE.md` |
| a project fact collaborators should have | project `CLAUDE.md` |
| a project fact that is yours alone (paths, URLs) | `CLAUDE.local.md` |
| needed only when touching certain files | a path-scoped rule |
| a multi-step procedure for one kind of task | a **skill** (module 6), not memory |
| something that must happen regardless | a **hook** (module 7), not memory |
| a correction you gave, or a preference | auto memory, written by Claude |

--

For auto memory, the harness's own rules: one fact per file; nothing the repo already records; link related memories; update, don't duplicate; delete what turns out wrong; verify a named file or flag still exists before recommending it.

---
name: lessons-library

# The Lessons-Library Pattern

A global file that keeps every lesson passes 200 lines within months. Adherence drops, and every request pays for it.

--

The split:

1. **The always-loaded file** keeps rules for every task plus a short **index**: one line per area, saying *when* to read it.
2. **Each area's playbook** is its own file (`~/.claude/lessons/latex.md`), read in full before a task in that area.
3. **New lessons go to the area file**, not the index. Old one-offs go to an archive.

--

This is module 4's cost lever on the memory side: pay for the index every request, pay for the playbook only when the task needs it. And a short index is one Claude actually consults.

---

# The End-of-Session Ritual

A session that learned something writes it down before `/clear`.

--

Codified here as a skill with a trigger token: refresh **local** project memory and the **global** instruction file, de-personalized; suggest a skill for any workflow that repeated; offer a tailored `NEXT SESSION` note to paste into the next session. The token is the go-ahead. The skill does not ask again.

--

Mid-session version: when the context is getting expensive, say so and offer the refresh before continuing. Same moment you would suggest `/clear`.

--

A sibling habit for confusions: when the user says "I don't understand X", log it (date, concept, what was unclear). Before explaining anything in that family later, add detail and a concrete example pre-emptively. The log tunes how to explain; it is not a verdict on anyone.

---
name: missing-1

# Where Memory Goes Missing (1): The Key Changed

The memory directory's `<key>` is derived from the path. A harness update changed the derivation once (observed 2026-06: `My_Project` became `My-Project`).

--

The old store became invisible. An empty one auto-created at the new key. Symptom: "my project memory vanished", with the files intact under a sibling key.

--

```bash
find ~/.claude/projects -maxdepth 2 -type d -name memory | \
  while read d; do echo "[$(ls -A "$d" | wc -l)] $d"; done
```

Compare with the key named in the session-start reminder. Fix: a **real directory** at the live key, not a symlink (recall does not traverse one). Verify end to end:

```bash
claude -p "State one fact from your memory index, or reply NO INDEX."
```

---

# Where Memory Goes Missing (2): Cloud Sessions

A session on claude.ai sees the repo clone and the account. Not this machine's `~/.claude`:

- no user `CLAUDE.md`, no `~/.claude/rules/`
- no `~/.claude/skills/`, no hooks from user settings
- no auto memory

--

What works:

- commit project rules and skills **into the repo**: `.claude/rules/`, `.claude/skills/`, project `CLAUDE.md`
- have cloud sessions write their memory to a committed `.claude/memory/` (project notes plus a global inbox) that the next local session drains into the real stores

--

Check portability before moving a skill to the cloud: most skills here need this machine (sandbox paths, `latexmk`, Ghostscript, `pbcopy`).

---

# Summary

| Layer | Loads | Budget | Drill proves it with |
|---|---|---|---|
| user `CLAUDE.md` | every session | share of 200 lines | headless probe: GLOBAL |
| project `CLAUDE.md` | every session in repo | under 200 lines | probe: TRIPS |
| `CLAUDE.local.md` | with the project file | small | probe: LAPTOP |
| path rule | when a matching file is touched | per rule | NONE, then SCOPED after reading an R file |
| lesson file | when the index line says | any | PLAYBOOK |
| auto memory | index every session | 200 lines / 25 KB | edit one, see it persist |

--

Next: a multi-step procedure does not belong in any of these rows. That is a skill.
